findings.title: Nil loop drive falls through to rhs[-1] panic
findings.message: The drive mode is chosen by `loopDrive != nil` instead of by the sweep parameter. In loop mode `sourceIndex` stays -1. If `openLoopControl` returns a nil or empty slice with no error, the code falls through to `rhs[-1] = 1` and panics with an index out of range. A drive vector longer than `len(jac)` would also panic.
findings.suggestion: Choose the branch from `plan.settings.Parameter == "loop-frequency"`, or from a boolean set alongside `loopDrive`. In the loop branch, check that `len(loopDrive) == len(jac)` and return an error if it is not, before the frequency loop starts.

findings.title: Unbounded crossing loop on untrusted phase data
findings.message: `loopMargins` is also called from `validateLoopMargins` on loaded, untrusted records. The odd-180 crossing loop advances one turn at a time from `lo` to `hi`. A segment with a huge phase span runs for an enormous number of iterations. At magnitudes like 1e300, `turn++` no longer changes the float, so the loop never ends. Unless every caller validates phase bounds and continuity before this point, a crafted project file can hang the service. The function also indexes `Values[0]` and `Values[1]` without checking the length.
findings.suggestion: Guard `loopMargins` before the crossing loop. Reject or skip points with non-finite or out-of-range phase, or a per-segment phase jump larger than about 360°. Also check `len(a.Values) >= 2` before indexing. Alternatively, have `validateLoopMargins` verify point bounds before calling `loopMargins`.

findings.title: Failure message may print a pointer address
findings.message: `op.Error` is probably a pointer (elsewhere the code uses `op.Error.Message`). If so, `t.Fatal(op.Error)` prints only an address or nil. A failing sweep would then give no useful diagnostic.
findings.suggestion: Print the error contents, for example `t.Fatalf("agent loop sweep failed: %+v", op.Error)`. This also adds context to the message.

findings.title: Marshal error ignored in test
findings.message: The test ignores the error from `json.Marshal`. If marshaling fails, the dispatch gets nil params and the test fails with a misleading mismatch instead of the real cause.
findings.suggestion: Check the error and call `t.Fatal(err)` if it is non-nil.

findings.title: Default settings can be invalid when no samples cover the interval
findings.message: Defaults are built from `r.LastSampleTime`. If a recording has a positive duration but no samples, or its last sample is at t=0, `End` and `Hold` both become 0. The docs require a positive hold that fits the covered interval, so the very first selection sends an invalid set command. The user sees a failure instead of a clear unavailable message.
findings.suggestion: Before offering probe options, check `r.LastSampleTime > 0`. If it is not, return a quiet unavailable node, mirroring the `Duration <= 0` branch. Otherwise clamp `Hold` to a positive minimum.
findings.evidence:
p.End = math.Min(r.Duration, r.LastSampleTime)
			p.Initial, p.Final, p.Tolerance, p.Hold = 0, 1, .02, math.Min(.002, p.End/10)

findings.title: Closure captures loop variable f
findings.message: The `Change` closures capture the range variable `f`. If the module's go directive is older than 1.22, every closure shares the final iteration's `f` (hold). Editing any field would then write `Hold` and compare against the wrong value.
findings.suggestion: Confirm go.mod targets Go 1.22 or later. Otherwise add `f := f` at the top of the loop body.

findings.title: Possible nil dereference of Sine in example graph
findings.message: `Sine` is used elsewhere as a nillable pointer (for example `p.Sine = nil`). If the base follower example's VIN is not a sine source, this line dereferences a nil pointer and panics when the example is built.
findings.suggestion: Check that `Sine` is non-nil before setting the amplitude, or initialize it explicitly.

findings.title: Target-not-found error omits loop-frequency targets
findings.message: The new `loop-frequency` target domain was added to `sweepTargets`. The 'target not found' error still lists only the old target kinds, so the message misleads users who pick a loop target on a component without dynamics.
findings.suggestion: Mention loop-frequency targets in the error message.
findings.evidence: return plan, fmt.Errorf("choose an existing DC bias, resistance, wiper or AC frequency target")

fix.before: return plan, fmt.Errorf("choose an existing DC bias, resistance, wiper or AC frequency target")
fix.after: return plan, fmt.Errorf("choose an existing DC bias, resistance, wiper, AC frequency or loop-frequency target")

findings.title: Published schema advertises descending ranges, but loop sweeps reject them
findings.message: The detailed schema says descending ranges are allowed for every parameter. Admission now rejects descending bands for `loop-frequency` ("loop sweep requires an ascending positive frequency band"). Clients or agents that trust the published relation will build settings that get refused. The test also had to special-case this.
findings.suggestion: Add a relation saying descending ranges are not allowed when `parameter=loop-frequency`, e.g. `{"operator": "ascending", "fields": ["start","stop"], "when": "parameter=loop-frequency"}`. Alternatively, note the exception in the start/stop descriptions.

findings.title: Set action skips time-input normalization used by query
findings.message: `stepResponseQueryLocked` passes its input through `normalizeTimeInput` before decoding, but `setStepResponseLocked` decodes the raw params directly. The same settings payload (for example, time values with units) may therefore be accepted by the query and rejected or misread by the set action.
findings.suggestion: Normalize time input in `setStepResponseLocked` the same way the query does, unless the caller already does this.

findings.title: stepQuery ignores marshal error and uses unchecked type assertion
findings.message: The helper discards the json.Marshal error and uses an unchecked type assertion on r.Result. A result type change makes the test panic instead of failing with a clear message.
findings.suggestion: Check the Marshal error and use the comma-ok assertion, calling t.Fatalf on mismatch.

findings.title: Capability schema check can panic and ignores unmarshal error
findings.message: caps[0] is indexed without a length check, so an empty result panics instead of failing the test. The json.Unmarshal error is also discarded, so a malformed schema is reported only as a missing contract.
findings.suggestion: Assert that len(caps) > 0 and check the Unmarshal error.
